meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-22, Time: 15:00 PDT, Duration: 42 minutes; Location: Zoom; Redwood: Maya Chen (AE), Rafael Ortiz (SE), Priya Kumar; Customer: Samir Patel (CTO), Laura Kim (ML Eng), Ethan Brooks (Infra), Jia Nguyen (Prod)
summary: Discovery focused on NorthBay's plan to exit a managed OpenAI + in-house vLLM stack; key concerns were eval parity, latency tail, KV cache behavior, and private deployment (VPC/KMS). Redwood AE/SE outlined Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs and proposed a focused benchmark to validate parity and routing policies.
topics: Current stack and pain points (OpenAI costs, vLLM maintenance)
Eval parity and quality regression risk
Serving topology: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
Performance: latency SLOs, tail latency, batching and KV cache
Security & compliance: SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
00:00:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:00:10 Speaker 2 (Samir): samir here, laura and ethan with me.
00:00:14 Speaker 3 (Laura): hi all.
00:00:16 Speaker 2 (Samir): we ran a little late so appreciate the time.
00:00:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): of course. goal for today is to understand your migration drivers - cost, latency, control - and propose a short benchmark. rafael will jump into infra questions.
00:00:33 Speaker 4 (Rafael): thanks maya. laura, can you give us a 2-3 minute on current setup? you mentioned openai for prod and vLLM for some on-prem experiments?
00:00:44 Speaker 3 (Laura): yeah so prod uses OpenAI - mostly chat/generation, embeddings elsewhere. costs spiked after last q because of volume. we also run vLLM on a few DGX nodes for reduced cost on long prompts but it's a maintenance headache.
00:00:58 Speaker 5 (Ethan): and network egress is painful. we're in a single cloud region with strict firewall and limited outbound. that's part of why private or VPC options matter.
00:01:08 Speaker 4 (Rafael): got it. what are your success criteria for a migration? like latency P95/P99, cost per 1k tokens, and qualitative parity?
00:01:18 Speaker 2 (Samir): p95 under 350ms for short chat messages, p99 under 1.4s ideally; cost needs to be at least 25% better than current openai spend or we don't justify the lift. parity: prompts used for product must not regress in top-of-funnel conversion.
00:01:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay solid. quick question on evals: do you have a fixed prompt set / golden outputs?
00:01:39 Speaker 3 (Laura): yes we have ~1200 prompt pairs — some are creative, some are retrieval-augmented. we compare at exact/semantic and human-rated quality.
00:01:47 Speaker 4 (Rafael): perfect, that helps. where are those stored? s3?
00:01:51 Speaker 3 (Laura): s3, we'll share.
00:01:54 Speaker 1 (Maya): great. now on hosting: Redwood hosted API gives fastest time to value; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools; Private gives VPC/on-prem. the choice depends on your egress and compliance needs.
00:02:07 Speaker 2 (Samir): our infosec is picky - SOC2 is baseline, and we need KMS integration and audit logs. also possible data residency in eu for some clients.
00:02:17 Speaker 4 (Rafael): all supported. KMS, HSM connectors, and per-tenant audit logs are in Private and Dedicated; hosted can be used with strict contracts for certain cases. we'll share the security pack.
00:02:28 Speaker 3 (Laura): can we talk about model variants — we use a trimmed tgi build for speed. how does Redwood handle vLLM and tgi parity?
00:02:36 Speaker 4 (Rafael): two parts: runtime parity and tokenization/decoder differences. runtime: our serving runtime is optimized for mainstream model families; for vLLM/TGI artifacts we do a compatibility shim, identify kernel differences, and run a calibration suite. sometimes outputs differ due to tokenizer, sampling seeds, or FP quantization.
00:02:54 Speaker 5 (Ethan): so for our long prompt flows with KV cache benefits, will you preserve KV behavior? we've seen context window optimizations in vLLM that rely on custom cache hooks.
00:03:03 Speaker 4 (Rafael): yes we have KV cache management and can replicate prefix caching semantics, but we'd validate with your prompt set. caching behavior is often the reason long-run token cost is lower.
00:03:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): also routing policies: you can split by routing policy — low latency routes to Dedicated, fall back to Hosted variants for overflow or to cheaper quantized models.
00:03:24 Speaker 2 (Samir): important for us because traffic is spiky with scheduled analytics runs. autoscaling burst is a must.
00:03:30 Speaker 4 (Rafael): Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale rules; we can set conservative warm pools to reduce p99 spikes.
00:03:36 Speaker 3 (Laura): about quantization — some of our models use 8-bit quant; does that materially change output quality? we had buttoned-down tests on tgi with 8-bit and saw small style shifts.
00:03:47 Speaker 4 (Rafael): quantization can shift probabilities; for many applications it's fine, but we always run an AB and human eval. Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles per-model/workload.
00:03:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): price note: quantized Dedicated is cheaper than full fp and cheaper than hosted for heavy throughput. we'll put numbers in the sheet.
00:04:07 Speaker 2 (Samir): security again — can we run Redwood in our VPC with no internet egress?
00:04:12 Speaker 4 (Rafael): yes, Private deploy supports air-gapped on-prem or VPC with private control plane. you'll still get the console via peering and we can set up a bastion for support.
00:04:21 Speaker 5 (Ethan): latency-wise, if we run in our region on prem GPU, what's the expected difference vs. current vLLM?
00:04:27 Speaker 4 (Rafael): should be similar or better due to attention kernel optimizations and batching. We'll need to see your sequence length distribution; long sequences benefit more from our KV and kernel selection.
00:04:37 Speaker 3 (Laura): about eval parity, we need automated regression alerts tied to a holdout prompt set — does Redwood support that?
00:04:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes Redwood Optimize + Console have quality monitoring, you can configure eval delta alerts and auto-rollback.
00:04:51 Speaker 2 (Samir): any gotchas migrating from OpenAI's API surface? we use function calling and streaming heavily.
00:04:58 Speaker 4 (Rafael): we support streaming and function-calling semantics; minor differences in function schemas sometimes come up. we'll map your API calls and build compatibility adapters where needed.
00:05:08 Speaker 3 (Laura): sample size for benchmarking — how much throughput do you need from us?
00:05:12 Speaker 4 (Rafael): for parity runs, ~1k-2k prompts across short and long families is usually enough; to check latency tails, run with production-like concurrency or synthetic traffic generator.
00:05:24 Speaker 1 (Maya): proposed pilot: 2-week scoped pilot. week 1: dry-run parity on 1k prompts in staging; week 2: production-like throughput test and routing validation. any blockers?
00:05:34 Speaker 2 (Samir): timeline ok. budget question — is there an eval fee?
00:05:38 Speaker 1 (Maya): we usually do a small pilot credit plus optional paid pilot for dedicated infra. i'll include options.
00:05:44 Speaker 3 (Laura): about logs and PII — can we redact or never store user prompt fields? we need to satisfy GDPR.
00:05:51 Speaker 4 (Rafael): yes you can configure redaction rules and retention windows; private deployments can be set to never persist request bodies.
00:05:58 Speaker 5 (Ethan): perf instrumentation — we need trace ids propagated through our stack.
00:06:02 Speaker 4 (Rafael): tracing hooks exist; we can accept custom trace ids and Surface per-request token accounting.
00:06:10 Speaker 3 (Laura): ok let's talk model catalog. we have a custom fork of an open decoder model via TGI. will you onboard custom model artifacts?
00:06:18 Speaker 4 (Rafael): yes we onboard customer artifacts; repackaging might be required. sometimes tokenizers differ and we re-run a tokenizer-mapping step. expect 1-2 days for packaging + a calibration suite.
00:06:30 Speaker 2 (Samir): cost question: if we keep some traffic on OpenAI for critical flows and route bulk to Redwood, can you support hybrid routing?
00:06:39 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes hybrid routing is common — we support traffic split by route, model, or policy. You can tier traffic by priority.
00:06:47 Speaker 3 (Laura): any previous customers who moved from a vLLM/TGI stack we can reference?
00:06:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): we have a few — i'll share anonymized case studies. one was a healthcare customer who moved to Dedicated.
00:06:58 Speaker 2 (Samir): compliance: do you offer SOC2 and ISA attestation?
00:07:03 Speaker 4 (Rafael): SOC2 type II yes, plus ISO in process; for private we do more on site audits.
00:07:09 Speaker 3 (Laura): about token accounting — we need token-level cost breakdowns per route.
00:07:13 Speaker 1 (Maya): Console provides token-level cost + latency breakdowns per model/route.
00:07:18 Speaker 5 (Ethan): what about cold-starts for large models that take time to load? we run jobs that spike.
00:07:23 Speaker 4 (Rafael): we recommend warm pools and pre-warmed slots for known scheduled spikes; also model sharding and fast checkpoint restore help.
00:07:33 Speaker 2 (Samir): ok one last technical: in our TGI experiments we saw tokenization drift — paraphrase answers changed style. how do you quantify 'no regression'?
00:07:42 Speaker 4 (Rafael): combination of automated metrics (ROUGE/BLEU/semantic similarity) plus a human rating for a held-out critical subset. we can also keep a canary route to OpenAI for a side-by-side comparison for the first month.
00:07:56 Speaker 3 (Laura): side-by-side is important. we'll want to see outputs in UI and diff tool.
00:08:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): ok i'll include a sample diff report in the follow-up.
00:08:06 Speaker 2 (Samir): logistic: firewall IP ranges, support SLA, and escalation paths?
00:08:11 Speaker 4 (Rafael): we have published IP ranges, we include an SLA for Dedicated/Private, and an escalation roster. will send those docs.
00:08:20 Speaker 3 (Laura): are there any features we won't get in Private?
00:08:23 Speaker 4 (Rafael): Private sometimes lags newest hosted features by a small window but most core runtime and Console features are there.
00:08:31 Speaker 1 (Maya): to recap: we'll share pricing, security pack, case studies, and a benchmark plan. NorthBay will share prompts, baseline outputs, and egress constraints. proposed follow up week of 6/1 for perf review.
00:08:48 Speaker 2 (Samir): sounds good. thanks.
00:08:51 Speaker 3 (Laura): thanks everyone.
00:08:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
00:08:56 Speaker 6 (System): meeting ended.
